title: Route new form and email leads into Close with dedupe, scoring and a review-gated follow-up
buyer: An SMB or agency already on Zapier (post price-hike) whose website-form and inbox leads leak between tools and the CRM.

trigger.why: A raw catch hook accepts any form, landing page or email parser's JSON, so one Zap serves every lead source instead of one Zap per source app.
trigger.idempotency: The hook fires once per POST; the dedupe step below is what makes a re-delivered POST safe.

steps.action: Text > Lowercase, then Trim, on the email field
steps.why: Normalize the email once so dedupe and the CRM upsert key on the same value.
steps.idempotency: Pure transform - no side effect, safe on replay.

steps.action: Find Contact - search by the normalized email
steps.why: Read the CRM before writing to choose create vs update and to honor dedupe.

steps.action: Numbers > Spreadsheet-Style Formula, scoring the lead from the rule table in this spec's scoring.rules
steps.why: A declared rule table keeps routing explainable and re-testable; the offline replay evaluates the same table.

steps.action: Route on the dedupe verdict and the score band
steps.why: Separates hot (write + draft), nurture (write), cold and duplicate (log only) without a second Zap.

steps.action: Create Contact / Update Contact (upsert) keyed on the normalized email
steps.why: One contact record per lead; a re-run updates the same record instead of adding a duplicate.
steps.idempotency: Keyed on the normalized email - replayed runs converge on one record.

steps.action: Create Draft - the follow-up email, never sent
steps.why: Outreach stays human-approved; the Zap stages the draft and stops.
steps.idempotency: One draft per hot lead, keyed on the contact id.

steps.action: Send Channel Message - the run digest
steps.why: One digest per run tells the owner exactly what moved.
steps.idempotency: The digest is emitted once per run, after routing settles.

steps.action: Create Spreadsheet Row - append the run-log row
steps.why: An append-only audit row per lead.
steps.idempotency: Keyed on lead id; duplicate verdicts are logged, never re-written to the CRM.

failure_branch.action: Custom error handler > Send Channel Message to the ops channel
failure_branch.detail: Attach a Zapier error handler to s2, s5, s6 and s8. The handler posts the lead id, the failing step and the error text to the ops channel and stops the branch. An errored step emits no output, so downstream mappings are intentionally empty.
failure_branch.idempotency: One alert per errored run; the handler does not retry the failed write.

test_cases.name: happy path
test_cases.input: a complete lead: large company, a demo request, a phone and a long message
test_cases.expected: score lands in the hot band -> CRM upsert + Gmail draft + log row

test_cases.name: missing data
test_cases.input: a lead with a blank email
test_cases.expected: the missing-data branch alerts and writes nothing to the CRM

test_cases.name: duplicate
test_cases.input: a second lead carrying an email already seen in the same batch
test_cases.expected: the duplicate branch skips the CRM write and the draft

test_cases.name: failure alert
test_cases.expected: the error handler posts the alert to the ops channel and the branch stops

derived_fields.phone: true when phone is a non-empty string

rules.why: a company big enough to have a buying process

honest_limit: Zapier has no credential-free one-click demo. A public Zap template cannot contain Formatter, Paths, Code or Webhooks steps and never runs for a visitor without their own account, so this workflow ships as the owner's own Zap and the deterministic steps are proven by the offline replay (replay.py) over the bundled fixture. The Zapier test-mode screenshots are owner-supplied at publish.
